messages.subject: choosing a model
parts:
Hi Chris,

I am crunching home ranges using ctmm for goitered gazelle in Mongolia.  I have the data parsed by year, season, year-season, etc.  When I run the home ranges, sometimes I get OU anistrophic as the best model, sometimes OUF anistrophic, sometimes IID.  Does it matter if you are using different models to calculate home ranges or do you need to stay with one model.  OUF anistrophic is usually the second choice when OU anistrophic is first.

Also, sometimes the 'guess' parameter does not show up when I execute the code.  I close R and re-open, but that does not fix it.  Any ideas?

Thanks, Nanette.

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: choosing a model
parts:
Hi Nanette,

You always want to condition AKDE on the best model. The best model can be different if either the movement is different or the sampling is different. If its the latter case, then that isn't a statement about what the animal is or isn't doing, but what you can or can't resolve from the data.

With ctmm.guess, be careful to either do this

GUESS <- ctmm.guess(DATA,interactive=FALSE)

or this

ctmm.guess(DATA) # click 'save' when finished

but not this

GUESS <- ctmm.guess(DATA)

Best,
Chris
